hero.headline: Aether Mocker
hero.tagline:
Software engineer and UX designer building
tools that respect the people using them —
from first sketch to shipped system.

about.label: § 01 — About
about.title: About Me
about.text: I'm a software engineer and UX designer working at the seam between research and implementation. I care about the parts of a product that are easy to skip — the empty states, the error messages, the way a form feels on a phone. My background is in computer science and psychology, which is a roundabout way of saying I'm equally interested in why people do things and how to build the thing they'll do it with.

education.note: Capstone: pilot-builder tooling for the Athletics Department. Undergraduate research in HCI and decision-making.
Foundations in data structures, discrete math, and web development.

items.title: Undergraduate Research — HCI Lab
items.desc: Designed and ran a study on decision-making in scheduling tools. Built the study apparatus as a web app, analyzed results in R, and co-authored a paper on interface defaults.

items.title: Front-End Engineering Intern
items.desc: Built accessible component primitives for a design system used across three product teams. Wrote the migration guide that moved 40+ screens off deprecated patterns.

blocks.label: Context
blocks.title: University of Portland Athletics Department
blocks.text: The department managed pilot schedules in spreadsheets that had drifted out of sync with the actual flight rules. I built a tool that encoded those rules and made conflicts visible before they became problems.

blocks.label: My Role
blocks.title: Full-stack development & UX research
blocks.text: Ran stakeholder interviews with three coordinators, observed two scheduling sessions, designed the interface in Figma, then built it in React and Node. Shipped to internal users in spring 2026.

blocks.label: Outcome
blocks.title: Scheduling time cut from hours to minutes
blocks.text: Coordinators reported that conflict detection caught issues they would previously have discovered on the day of the flight. The tool is still in use and has been handed off to a student team.

blocks.label: Context
blocks.title: Center for International Study
blocks.text: Prospective students had no way to compare study-abroad programs geographically. The existing catalog was a PDF sorted alphabetically.

blocks.label: My Role
blocks.title: Design & front-end development
blocks.text: Mapped program data to a Leaflet map, designed the filter interaction, and built the accessibility layer so the map was usable by keyboard and screen reader.

blocks.label: Outcome
blocks.title: Advisor meetings up 30%
blocks.text: Advisors reported that students arrived at meetings already knowing which programs they wanted to discuss — the map did the first-pass filtering for them.

list.name: Cribbage Game
list.desc: Browser-based card game with AI opponent (2023-2024)

blocks.label: Context
blocks.title: Personal project
blocks.text: I wanted a project that would force me to think about state machines and game AI without a framework doing the work for me.

blocks.label: My Role
blocks.title: Everything
blocks.text: Rules engine, AI opponent (minimax with hand-evaluation heuristics), UI, and animation. Vanilla JS, no dependencies.

blocks.label: Outcome
blocks.title: Shipped and playable
blocks.text: The AI beats me about 60% of the time, which feels like the right ratio for a game you play against yourself.

blocks.label: Context
blocks.title: Internal tooling at internship
blocks.text: Three product teams had diverged on button, input, and modal implementations. The design team had a Figma library; engineering had nothing matching it.

blocks.label: My Role
blocks.title: Component author & migration lead
blocks.text: Built the primitive components, wrote the codemod that migrated existing call sites, and ran the office hours where teams could bring questions.

blocks.label: Outcome
blocks.title: 40+ screens migrated in 6 weeks
blocks.text: New feature work no longer required a design review to check whether the button matched the spec — the component was the spec.

list.name: Plant Care Logging App
list.desc: Personal project — habit tracking for plants (2026)

blocks.label: Context
blocks.title: Personal project
blocks.text: I kept killing plants. I wanted to understand whether the problem was the plants or my memory.

blocks.label: My Role
blocks.title: Design & development
blocks.text: Built a logging app with local-first storage, a small reminder system, and a UI that assumes you're holding a watering can in one hand.

blocks.label: Outcome
blocks.title: Plants alive, mostly
blocks.text: The app reduced missed waterings by enough that I now have more plants than I started with. This is both a success and a problem.

approach.label: How I Work
approach.heading: Start with the problem, not the brief.
approach.text: Every project begins with listening — to users, to constraints, to the parts of the system that already exist. I'd rather ask a dumb question in week one than build the wrong thing in week six.

expect.label: What I Bring
items: Front-end implementation in React, vanilla JS, or whatever fits
